items.title: Docetaxel and SX-682 Trial for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing SX-682 (a new drug targeting immune cells) combined with docetaxel chemotherapy in patients with metastatic prostate cancer that has returned or spread. The trial is not yet recruiting and also includes patients with head and neck cancers. SX-682 is taken as a pill, and the study will evaluate safety and effectiveness.

items.title: Pembrolizumab Combinations in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing pembrolizumab (an immunotherapy) combined with various treatments including olaparib, docetaxel, enzalutamide, and others in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study has ten different treatment groups and is no longer recruiting new patients. It aims to find safe and effective combination approaches.

items.title: HLD-0915 Trial in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial evaluating HLD-0915, a new investigational drug, in patients with metastatic prostate cancer who have already received prior treatments. The study is actively recruiting and will assess both safety and how well the drug works. Additional prostate cancer patient groups may be included.

items.title: BNT324 vs Docetaxel Phase 3 Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing BNT324 (a new targeted therapy) to standard docetaxel chemotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with hormone therapy but not chemotherapy. The study is recruiting and will measure how long patients live without cancer progression and overall survival. This could establish a new treatment option.

items.title: STEAP1 CAR-T Cell Therapy Plus Enzalutamide Trial
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing STEAP1 CAR-T cell therapy (genetically modified immune cells that target prostate cancer) combined with enzalutamide in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This represents a novel immunotherapy approach using patients' own modified T cells to attack cancer. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Hormone Therapy in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 trial evaluating xaluritamig (an investigational immunotherapy) combined with darolutamide or abiraterone in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and focuses on determining safe doses and tolerability of these combinations in earlier-stage metastatic disease.

items.title: BMS-986365 Phase 3 Trial in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing BMS-986365 to physician's choice of standard therapy in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and will measure effectiveness and safety. This large trial could establish a new treatment standard if successful.

items.title: Xaluritamig Safety Study in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 1 trial determining the safety profile of xaluritamig in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and will establish the recommended dosing regimen for this investigational immunotherapy drug.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177 PSMA in mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial testing luxdegalutamide (a new hormone therapy) combined with Lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy compared to Lutetium-177 alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The study is no longer recruiting and will help determine the best dose for future trials. Patients must have received prior hormone therapy.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Phase 3 Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 3 trial comparing xaluritamig plus abiraterone to physician's choice of treatment (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not received chemotherapy. The study is recruiting and will measure overall survival as the primary outcome.

items.title: Nezastomig With or Without Cemiplimab in mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing REGN5678 (nezastomig) alone or combined with cemiplimab immunotherapy in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and will first find safe doses, then evaluate how well the treatments shrink tumors. Blood levels and side effects will also be monitored.

items.title: Lutetium-177 Dotatate for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial studying Lutetium-177 dotatate (a radioactive drug) in metastatic prostate cancer with neuroendocrine features. This treatment targets somatostatin receptors found on some neuroendocrine cancer cells and delivers radiation directly to them. The trial is recruiting and represents a novel approach for this aggressive variant.

items.title: Tinengotinib Combined With Hormone Therapy in mCRPC
items.summary: A Phase 1/2 trial testing tinengotinib (TT-00420) combined with abiraterone or enzalutamide in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and aims to determine if this combination is safe and causes few side effects. Tinengotinib targets specific growth pathways.

items.title: DNA Vaccines With Pembrolizumab in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: A Phase 2 trial comparing one versus two DNA vaccines (pTVG-HP and pTVG-AR) given with pembrolizumab immunotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Treatment continues for up to 2 years. The study tests whether two vaccines generate stronger immune responses than one, measured by PSA declines and tumor shrinkage.

items.title: Inflammation and Epigenetic Changes Drive Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research paper describes how chronic inflammation rewires gene activity in prostate cancer through NFκB and IL-6/STAT3 signaling pathways. These inflammatory signals work with androgen receptor signaling to promote tumor survival, spread, and resistance to treatment. Understanding these mechanisms may reveal new therapeutic targets for advanced disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Checkpoint Blockade Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study developed a next-generation nanoplasmid DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein highly expressed on prostate cancer cells). The vaccine generated strong immune responses and, when combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade, prevented tumor growth and lung metastases in research models. This approach may help overcome resistance to immunotherapy.

items.title: Sudden Liver Metastases After First Lutetium-177 PSMA Treatment
items.summary: A case report of a 63-year-old man with bone-predominant metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who developed widespread liver metastases after his first cycle of Lutetium-177 PSMA therapy. The liver disease was not visible on initial scans but appeared on post-treatment imaging, creating uncertainty about continuing therapy.

items.title: Theranostics in Nuclear Medicine: Evidence and Regulatory Context
items.summary: This review examines theranostic radiopharmaceuticals like Lutetium-177 dotatate and Lutetium-177 PSMA, which combine diagnosis and treatment. It discusses clinical trial design standards, regulatory approvals, dose optimization, toxicity assessment, and practical considerations for nuclear medicine physicians implementing these therapies in practice.

items.title: PSMA Theranostics in Prostate Cancer: Current Standards
items.summary: This article reviews the paradigm shift in prostate cancer management using PSMA-based theranostics. PSMA PET/CT provides superior diagnostic accuracy compared to conventional imaging, while Phase 3 trials have established the therapeutic benefit of Lutetium-177 PSMA in metastatic castration-resistant disease.

items.title: Automated Dosimetry for Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy Predicts Outcomes
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This study of 59 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients found that automated dosimetry (measuring radiation doses) from single SPECT/CT scans after Lutetium-177 PSMA treatment correlated with blood count changes and PSA responses. Bone marrow radiation dose predicted red blood cell declines, helping identify patients at risk for side effects.

items.title: Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy in Younger vs Older Prostate Cancer Patients
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This matched-pair study compared 51 patients age 65 or younger to 51 patients age 70 or older receiving Lutetium-177 PSMA therapy. Both age groups showed similar PSA responses, progression-free survival, overall survival, and safety profiles, suggesting the treatment is equally effective and safe in younger men.

items.title: Targeting PI3K/AKT Pathway in PTEN-Deficient Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review discusses how loss of the PTEN gene activates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in prostate cancer, promoting tumor growth and treatment resistance. The article explores using PTEN testing as a biomarker to identify patients who may benefit from drugs targeting this pathway.

items.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Efficacy in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 1,580 patients from 21 trials found that immune checkpoint inhibitors alone showed modest benefit in unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, with 1-year survival of 63% and 6-month progression-free survival of 41%. Combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors showed better outcomes than single-agent treatment.
